materials.reason: Bambu Lab's filament guide has no column for plain PETG: its columns are PLA, PETG HF, ABS, ASA, PC, the TPUs and the fibre-filled grades. PETG HF, a high-flow PETG and a product of PETG here (m141, D86), is its one unfilled PETG and the nearest column, so a PETG product whose own sheet and twin are silent reads it, labelled as the guide's. It is a high-flow grade's window (nozzle 230 to 260 °C, bed 60 to 80 °C), which a plain PETG's own sheet may set lower. Not PETG-CF, a column of its own, nor PETG-GF, -ESD, PCTG, CPE or PET, which the guide does not name.

method.rule: 2026-09-21. The V2 import (batches b01 to b33, docs/audits/2026-09-18-v2-import), the sweep of outlying values against their sheets, and an estimate per grade from the same model (D81). Family entries own no product. There is no weighted selection score: a goal ranks the candidates by a performance index computed product by product (D83). The date is for a reader; the release ID identifies the data and rules a page, scenario or export was made with (D96).
Materials Wiki, the legacy XLSM and synced project sources are read-only references. No workbook macros were executed or imported.
CPE/CoPE, TPC/TPEE and umbrella nylon records remain separate canonical rows. Shared formulation keys identify repeated commercial evidence, not independent tests.

Up to three technical grade samples per generic entry. Exact Bambu entries use their own TDS. Supplemental study grades carry R1 suffixes and are not procurement grades. Manufacturer-count shortfalls are explicit.

Official printer documentation for H2C routes. Manufacturer TDS/SDS for exact grades. Original studies for measured behaviour. Retailer evidence is used for prices, not technical properties. Wiki for selection concepts only.

Not published means absent from the sampled evidence, not proven absent from all literature. Insufficient comparable data means values cannot support the proposed comparison. Not applicable means the field does not apply: a requirement on it never passes and never fails, and with the materials that could not be checked included it hides the material, whether estimates are on or off (D148). Never use zero for missing data.

A product description is a manufacturer claim, not independent validation. Certifications are grade-, colour-, thickness- and application-specific. No food-contact or general safety approval is implied.

A material is shown as the spread of its products (D83): each number is the median of its products' comparable values, with their range, how many there are, and the product nearest the median named as typical. A comparable value is in the headline's direction, dry or unstated, at the headline's load. A tensile, flexural, impact or heat deflection value comes from a printed bar, said or implied by its document, read flat where it states no orientation (D172); density, glass transition and hardness, which are not a bar's, also take an unstated specimen. A bar no document describes as printed is set apart for good: shown and counted apart, never used to pass (D172), except for the heat deflection of an unfoamed plastic that cannot crystallise, which counts unless its document points to moulded or resin bars (D177). A heat deflection with no stated load is counted apart too, and reaches a decision only as a floor of the 0.45 MPa value, through a deciding row of the evidence ledger (CV63, D172); declared variants are counted apart as well. Only comparable values form a range, so incompatible standards, moisture states, preparation, load and orientation never mix. A material passes a requirement when one of its products meets every requirement at once.

XY and Z remain separate. A printed bar, said or implied by its document, that states no orientation is read flat, as makers print their test bars unless they say otherwise (D172); a Z value is only one its source says was upright. A bar no document describes as printed is no XY value either: it is set apart (D172). Printed, resin, filament and unspecified specimens cannot be treated as equivalent.

Tensile yield, break and unspecified-endpoint strength are separate. Flexural strength is not tensile strength. Charpy/Izod, notch state and energy-per-width versus energy-per-area are distinct. Impact does not substitute for KIC.
Keep HDT load, Tg, Vicat, melting and continuous-service ratings distinct. A TDS test-preparation anneal is not automatically a recommended part anneal. Dimensional change must be qualified.
Density g/cm³ ×1000 = kg/m³. Modulus MPa ×0.001 = GPa. Strength MPa remains MPa. Area-normalized impact remains kJ/m². No conversion from J/m without specimen geometry. CTE target is µm/m/K.
Raw ± term and ranges are retained separately. The source may not identify whether ± is standard deviation. Values with unresolved units/layout are quarantined and excluded from numeric summaries.

The exact product, 1.75 mm, one spool or refill, with its net filament mass printed: an in-stock regular price, before shipping. CAD from a Canadian storefront first (a Canadian retailer, a maker's Canadian store, or Amazon.ca where the seller is the maker's own store); where no Canadian shop in the sample lists the product, the maker's shop or a seller in USD, then in EUR (D113). Before tax: a EUR price has the VAT its page states taken off, and one whose rate is not printed is not comparable. Promotions visible separately. Bambu variant price must match an explicit MSRP or a verified single-unit regular header price with no promotion in that price block.

A product's price is the median of its own headline-sample listings, one offer per seller, which prevents colour-count bias: its Canadian listings where it has any, its foreign ones only where it has none. A material's price is the median of its plain products' prices (D83). Prefer spool and mass closest to 1 kg. Refills remain explicitly labelled. Grade-matched sample is not a whole-market lowest-price search.

Regular CAD/kg = regular price before VAT / net filament kg x the Bank of Canada rate for its currency (CAD: 1), to the cent. A 0.5 kg spool doubles CAD/kg relative to its spool price; a 0.75 kg spool divides by 0.75. Sale, bulk and unavailable offers do not enter a median. A converted price is marked wherever it is shown.

Price observations are snapshots, each with its access date; the sample spans the dates its listings were read. Stale-price threshold is 30 days from the fixed snapshot date, not a live TODAY calculation. Recheck stock and variant when buying.

One Bank of Canada daily rate per currency, CAD per unit, read from its Valet service as a fetched, hashed document (fx_rates.csv). The latest row per currency is in force, and every foreign listing of a release is compared at it, never at a rate of its own day. A foreign price says nothing about shipping to Canada, duty or Canadian stock, and never makes a product listed or buyable in Canada.
350°C nozzle, 120°C bed and 65°C active chamber, subject to nozzle and hotend route. A grade needing more is not approved merely because its polymer family appears in marketing material.
H2C-WIKI controls route-specific restrictions. PET-CF/PPA-CF/PPS-CF are left-only there. Soft TPU restrictions and promised firmware support are not treated as released support.

Do not mix high- and low-temperature groups. Low-temperature materials can soften in a hot chamber. PVA support pairing requires H2C-specific routing verification; generic soluble support guidance is insufficient. The low-temperature chamber guide limit is 45 °C, and pairing is verified per grade, not per family.

For sustained loads use grade/condition/time/temperature-specific creep or relaxation data. Short-term modulus and strength alone do not predict clamp-force retention or long-term deflection. See LOCAL-CREEP.

Study stress/cycle observations are not design allowables. A 1,000,000-cycle run-out is right-censored, not proof of infinite life. Preserve R, frequency, temperature and raster. Reinforcement does not guarantee improved fatigue. See LOCAL-FATIGUE.

Analyst rubric published here, not a manufacturer-measured score. 1: straightforward profile, little warping. 2: ordinary profile plus routine tuning. 3: drying/adhesion control central. 4: several material-specific constraints or advanced handling. 5: severe adhesion/warping or industrial thermal requirements. Higher means greater processing burden.

Only mapped where manufacturer guidance supports an anchor. PLA=1; PETG=2; ABS/ASA/PC/PA/soft TPU/soluble supports=4; unfilled PP=5. Reinforced, effect, hardness and brand variants do not inherit a numeric family rating. No universal chemical score.

Ratings are qualitative screening judgments, not H2C test results. Texture, tolerances, creep, fatigue and chemical endurance remain unscored where an anchored, grade-specific comparison is unavailable.
Density; kg/m³. MainUi D9; Database E:F. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Tensile modulus with direction/condition; GPa. MainUi D28; Database G:H. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Tensile yield strength; MPa. MainUi D46; Database I:J. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Tensile ultimate or source-labelled endpoint; MPa. MainUi D64; Database K:L. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Compression strength with failure criterion and conditioning; MPa. MainUi D82; Database M:N. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Elongation at break; preserve % and gauge/test method; %. MainUi D100; Database O:P. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
KIC or other declared fracture metric; never impact; MPa√m. MainUi D118; Database Q:R. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Coefficient of thermal expansion with direction and interval; µm/m/K. MainUi D137; Database S:T. Original min/max pairs; uncited numeric values are not imported.
Coverage is terminal: it reports gaps and conflicts but does not drive material or price calculations. A row with evidence is not a declaration that all properties are known.

PA66-CF, unfilled PA612 and PA612-GF lack verified exact-grade technical profiles in this sample, and PA66's two products are filed by inference (R225, R226). PLA Lite and PLA Silk carry third-party technical grade samples (eSUN PLA-Lite, Panchroma Silk PLA), not the original products. Full H2C routing/AMS validation is not established for every third-party grade.

Nozzle thermal limits, ventilation, solvent handling, dust and exact-grade SDS review remain necessary. Low odour and polymer food-contact statements do not establish a safe printed article or process.

Official H2C manual V1.0 January2026 was accessible again on2026-09-10; brittle-filament route restriction confirmed. Direct wiki refresh returned402 in the web reader, so the retrieved source snapshot is retained. Firmware-sensitive soft-TPU support remains conservatively unverified; confirm installed firmware before use.

"Published value (transcription corrected)" marks a row whose VALUE or UNIT was recovered from the cited source after an earlier parsing error, with the reasoning recorded in the row Notes. It is a re-read of the same source, never an inference from a different grade or from the literature. Such rows re-enter numeric summaries; rows that could not be recovered stay at "Unresolved unit / layout" and stay quarantined.

Nine of fifteen quarantined measurements were resolved by re-reading the cited TDS. Two conflicts were closed (IPCON PPA AMS wording, 3DXTECH PEEK temperature ranges - non-blocking because both exceed the 350/120/65 baseline). Four fatigue conflicts were confirmed as genuine source defects by recomputing the stated percentages against the stated ultimate strengths. Four items remain open: the iSANMATE rows (robots-disallowed, five measurements plus the PLA-GF composition and PEI/PEEK unit rows), the FormFutura PET hardness row (image-only PDF), and the Spectrum PCTG notched Izod row (defect verified present in the current TDS).

Official and current manufacturer evidence was checked for Bambu Lab, eSUN, Fillamentum, BASF Forward AM, Stratasys, 3DXTECH, Markforged, Essentium/Nexa3D, Polymaker, Prusa Research and Kimya/Airtech. Exact-grade identity was required for inserted values.

86 existing target-manufacturer source records were refetched or checked; every recorded hash matched fetched bytes. 1,333 existing numeric property rows were checked for their raw numbers in extracted current PDF text with zero missing numeric tokens. This detects stale files and many transcription errors, but not every possible semantic mislabel.

Current catalog products were not inserted merely because their family name looked similar. Closed-platform or over-sample candidates remain in the external research report unless an exact canonical mapping and evidence need justified a workbook grade.

A published nozzle, bed or chamber window is read against the H2C's 350 °C nozzle, 120 °C bed and 65 °C active chamber. At or below the limit: within. Starting at or below it and extending above: within, at the low end of the maker's window, where the H2C covers 5 °C or more of it, since a maker's window says any setting in it works; on the line, unresolved, where the H2C reaches only its bottom edge (D151). Wholly above: exceeds, or above recommended where the sheet only recommends it. "Not required", room temperature or "enclosure not needed" clear the chamber question without inventing a temperature. "Recommended" without a number, "-" in a TDS and no setpoint stay unknown. A chamber no product sheet, shared sheet or printer guide says anything about is read from the makers of its kind of plastic (chamber_need.csv): within where at least ten of them state one and at most one in ten asks above 65 °C, labelled with those counts; else unknown (D151). An enclosure is not an actively heated chamber.

Implemented after re-reading every cited source. Chamber rows missed at a page break were recovered from 14 Bambu TDS files whose SHA-256 matches this register. Four technical grade samples were added (eSUN PLA-Lite, Panchroma Silk PLA, Panchroma CoPE, Fiberon PET-GF15) and CoPE was separated from CPE. Sources that could not be retrieved contributed nothing. Research chamber bands are inference kept outside this workbook.

A grade whose Status is retired is kept as an audit record and is inactive: it is not in its material's grade list, its profiles leave the material's print summary and gates, and no active measurement, price, headline or use record may cite it. Status is the one place a retirement is recorded; Availability keeps what was recorded about buying the product, which a retirement does not change.

A headline none of a material's products publishes comparably may carry a material estimate, always shown as an estimate; with several products it is any one of them, so it carries the spread between products. Each product with no comparable value of its own carries its own estimate too (D81, D137). One Gaussian model per headline, on a log scale for density, stiffness, strength and elongation and in °C for heat deflection, takes every observation in the snapshot: products' values, their related measurements (another endpoint, direction, load or specimen, and resin data sheets) and its other grades, each converted to the headline's own semantics with a documented offset and spread refined from grades that publish both. Its structure is polymer identity within its chemical group, reinforcement by matrix, declared variants, test house and, for the heat deflection of polymers that crystallise while printing, the melting point; each material and product adds its own deviation. Melting point and glass transition limit heat deflection. The likely (80%) and plausible (95%) ranges are calibrated by hiding each material's typical product's value and predicting it back. An estimate never passes a requirement: under the materials that could not be checked, it orders those with not enough data and tags likely the ones whose likely range meets every open limit, and a product whose own plausible range wholly misses is unlikely to meet, listed and counted (D155). A material with products is judged product by product, so its material estimate is context and decides nothing; a product's own estimate may hide that product only where a back-test certifies it, and none is certified in this release. Only a material with no product on record is judged on its own estimate, which hides it, with the materials that could not be checked included and estimates on, when its plausible range and the part of it the back-test lets it screen on both wholly fail the requirement and no own measurement of that property could meet it (D48, D59, D148). Heat deflection does not apply to an elastomer (headline_definitions.csv Applies to): a value its own sheet publishes stays that sheet's measurement and never decides. Any value of a support product is not applicable unless its own sources publish one. Parameters: build/mappings/estimate-model.json; the documented conversions are rows of data/tables/conversions.csv (D157).

A resin supplier data sheet may be recorded for an identity no filament source characterises, as a study grade (R suffix) whose values are raw-material values from moulded specimens. It is never a headline or a procurement grade; it anchors estimates through a documented moulded-to-printed conversion.

A canonical name that is a family or an alias (PA, PA-CF, PA-GF, TPE; CoPA for PA6/66) has Scope "Family entry". It owns no product and carries no value; each commercial product is recorded once, under the most specific material it is. A product found under two materials is retired from the less specific one (its grade's Status retired), and its records are marked "Retired duplicate record" after proving each has an identical twin. Members: data/tables/family_members.csv.
Data-sheet values describe test specimens, not design allowables. Confirm the exact product, its conditioning and your part's geometry with your own print.

A material's headline is derived from its products, never chosen: each product's value is the one its own measurements give by rule (build/src/products.js: comparable before as published, printed before unstated, as printed before annealed, dry before unstated, its own data sheet first), and headlines.csv pins a product's value, with its reason, only where the rule chooses wrongly. A family entry has no values of its own and points at its members; a material none of whose products publishes a comparable value has insufficient comparable data.

A fibre-filled filament (carbon, glass, aramid or plant fibre) wears a brass nozzle whatever its sheet says. Where neither the product's own sheet, its twin's (D89) nor the printer maker's guide (D88) says what nozzle it needs, the selector treats it as abrasive: under "No hardened nozzle" it is unresolved, never passed. A source's own statement always wins, stricter or looser. This is the database's rule, not a source's statement; until m296 the import wrote it into each fibre profile's Abrasion / clogging cell (D121).

Notched Charpy (ISO 179) and notched Izod (ISO 180) are two tests. Charpy supports the bar at both ends and strikes it in the middle; Izod clamps the bar upright at one end and strikes its free end. Both report the energy absorbed per area of the notched section, in kJ/m², but the bars, notches and supports differ, so a Charpy value is not an Izod value. Each dot is one product's published value, and the two rows share a scale only so that a product can be found on both; no value is converted. Izod in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch width: it is listed with the results below, not drawn.

A tensile bar printed flat (XY) is pulled along its printed lines; a bar printed upright (Z) is pulled across its layers, so its result is how well the layers hold together, and is usually lower. Both are one test (ISO 527 or ASTM D638) on bars built differently: an XY value is not a Z value, and neither is converted. Modulus, strength and elongation at break each have their own scale, which the XY and Z rows share only so that a product can be found on both. A Z row compares only a bar the sheet says was pulled along Z. A printed bar whose sheet states no orientation is read flat and compared on the XY row (D172); a bar no document describes as printed can stand only on the XY row, drawn hollow and not compared, and a bar labelled XZ or ZX is drawn as Z only where its sheet says or shows it stood upright, or where its maker uses that label for its upright bar (Eryone's "X-Z"); any other is listed below, not drawn. Z as a share of XY is given only for a product whose two values are compared, from one document and in one state. Where a product publishes no XY value measured the way a requirement asks, its Z value still bounds the XY one from below: an upright bar is held by its layer bonds and is not meaningfully stiffer or stronger than a flat one, so XY is at least 0.79 times its Z modulus and 0.86 times its Z strength, the least any same-sheet pair here gives (the evidence ledger's floors, D153).

Heat deflection temperature (ISO 75, ASTM D648) is the temperature at which a loaded bar, heated steadily, bends by a set amount, under 0.45 MPa or under 1.8 MPa. The heavier load gives the lower temperature, so the two rows are two tests and neither is converted. The glass transition (Tg), usually measured by DSC on a few milligrams with no load, is where the polymer turns from glassy to rubbery: an amorphous plastic loses its stiffness above it, while a semicrystalline one can carry load well above it. All three are in °C and share a scale only so that a product can be found on each; none is a service temperature. A value whose sheet states no load can stand only on the 0.45 MPa row, drawn hollow and not compared. A bar no document describes as printed is drawn hollow too, unless its plastic cannot crystallise and is not foamed, and its document points to no moulded or resin bar (D172, D177). A product that publishes no 0.45 MPa value measured the way a requirement asks is still judged on its 1.8 MPa value where that already meets the limit: under the heavier load a bar deflects sooner, so its 0.45 MPa value is at least as high (the evidence ledger's floor, D153).

A flexural bar (ISO 178, ASTM D790) rests on two supports and is pressed in the middle, so its lower face is stretched and its upper face compressed. Printed flat (XY), its outer faces are printed lines along the bar; printed upright (Z), bending pulls the layer bonds apart at the outer face, and its result is usually lower. An XY value is not a Z value, and neither is converted. Modulus and strength each have their own scale, which the XY and Z rows share only so that a product can be found on both. A Z row compares only a bar the sheet says was printed upright. A printed bar whose sheet states no orientation is read flat and compared on the XY row (D172); a bar no document describes as printed can stand only on the XY row, drawn hollow and not compared, and a bar labelled XZ or ZX is drawn as Z only where its sheet says or shows it stood upright, or where its maker uses that label for its upright bar (Eryone's "X-Z"); any other is listed below, not drawn. Z as a share of XY is given only for a product whose two values are compared, from one document and in one state.

method.topic: How flexural and tensile results relate
method.rule: In a bending test the stress at the outer face is worked out from elastic beam theory. For a solid, uniform material that behaves alike in tension and compression, the flexural modulus is its tensile modulus. A printed bar departs from that: bending loads its outer perimeters most and its infill and layer bonds least, and a short span adds shear, so its two moduli can differ by tens of per cent either way. Flexural strength is usually above tensile strength, for unfilled plastics often by a third to three quarters: only the outer face reaches the peak stress, so less material is at risk of a flaw, and once the plastic yields the elastic formula overstates the stress it reports. Where the bar does not break, sheets report the stress at 3.5 % or 5 % strain, listed as the stress at conventional deflection. Neither value converts into the other. Where a product publishes no tensile modulus measured the way a requirement asks, its flexural modulus bounds the tensile one between 0.46 and 1.93 times, the widest any same-sheet pair of solid, non-rubbery bars here gives, and decides only where that whole band lies on one side of the limit (the evidence ledger, D153).
Makers rarely give the concentration, temperature or duration: treat them as indications, not design data.

The H2C takes 1.75 mm filament (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-20). A product's Diameter is what its documents print: 1.75 mm where a document or a listing of it gives that diameter, 2.85 mm only (or 3 mm only) where they give only a larger one, Not published where none prints a diameter. A product found only in a larger diameter is kept and counted, as its values describe its polymer as printed; its detail in the drawer and its card on the material's page say that only that filament was found (D175).

properties.name: Impact strength
properties.description: An impact result whose test is unclear: the sheet names no test, or names both (a "Charpy" label beside an Izod standard, an "Izod" label beside ISO 179). Kept apart from Charpy and Izod and never compared; where the rest of the sheet points to one test, a reviewer's reading is written beside the value (impact_test_guesses.csv). A result whose own label or standard names the test is filed under that test.

properties.name: Mould shrinkage
properties.description: How much a moulded or printed part shrinks as it cools, to ISO 294-4 or ASTM D955. A sheet that prints it parallel and normal to the flow publishes two rows.

properties.name: Volume resistivity
properties.description: Resistance through the body of the material, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257. It is what separates a conductive or ESD grade from an insulating one.

properties.name: Surface resistivity
properties.description: Resistance across the surface, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257.

properties.name: Dielectric strength
properties.description: The field a material holds before it breaks down, to IEC 60243 or ASTM D149.

properties.name: Relative permittivity
properties.description: The dielectric constant, to IEC 60250 or ASTM D150. A sheet states the frequency it was measured at, which the row keeps as its test condition.

properties.name: Comparative tracking index
properties.description: The voltage at which a wetted, contaminated surface begins to track, to IEC 60112. A sheet may print it as a stage rather than a voltage; only a voltage is a value here.

properties.name: Oxygen index
properties.description: The least oxygen concentration that sustains burning, to ISO 4589 or ASTM D2863. A flammability class (UL 94 V-0, HB) is a certification claim, not this.

properties.name: Tear strength
properties.notApplicableReason: A tear test (ISO 34, ASTM D624) is run on elastomers and on tough, drawing plastics such as the polyolefins; a rigid filament is not tear-tested, and its sheet never prints one.
properties.description: The force per thickness that tears a specimen, to ISO 34 or ASTM D624. Published for elastomers and films.

properties.name: Abrasion loss
properties.description: The volume a standard abrasive removes, to ISO 4649 or DIN 53516. A smaller number wears less.

properties.name: Compression set
properties.notApplicableReason: Compression set is how much of a squeeze a rubbery material keeps; a rigid plastic is not tested for it.
properties.description: How much of a compression an elastomer keeps after the load is taken off, to ISO 815 or ASTM D395. A sheet states the time and temperature, which the row keeps as its test conditions.

properties.name: Poisson's ratio
properties.description: How much a specimen narrows as it is stretched.

properties.name: Decomposition temperature
properties.description: Where the material begins to break down rather than melt, by thermogravimetry (ISO 11358). A sheet states the mass loss it is quoted at, commonly 5 %, which the row keeps as its test condition.

properties.name: Tensile stress at 5 % elongation
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 5 % elongation, as a sheet prints it ("Tensile Strength @ 5% Strain"). Not a strength: no headline reads it, and it is never compared with one (D122).

properties.name: Tensile stress at 10 % elongation
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 10 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

properties.name: Tensile stress at 100 % elongation
properties.notApplicableReason: Only a material that stretches past 100 % has a stress at 100 % elongation: an elastomer, or a polyolefin that yields and draws; a rigid filament breaks long before.
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 100 % elongation: an elastomer's "100 % modulus" (ISO 37, ASTM D412, or ISO 527 on an elastomer). Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

properties.name: Tensile stress at 200 % elongation
properties.notApplicableReason: Only an elastomer stretches to 200 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 200 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

properties.name: Tensile stress at 300 % elongation
properties.notApplicableReason: Only an elastomer stretches to 300 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 300 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

properties.name: Tensile stress at 400 % elongation
properties.notApplicableReason: Only an elastomer stretches to 400 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
properties.description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 400 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

properties.name: Tensile impact strength
properties.description: A tensile-impact test (ASTM D1822, ISO 8256): a bar pulled to break by a pendulum. Neither a Charpy nor an Izod result, and compared with neither.

properties.name: Fibre content
properties.appliesToText: Modifier / filler: Carbon fibre | Glass fibre | Aramid fibre | Natural fibre
properties.notApplicableReason: Fibre content is the share of reinforcing fibre a maker adds to the plastic; a material sold without a fibre load has none to state.
properties.description: The fibre load the maker states, by weight unless the row says otherwise; a range is kept as printed.

relations.basis: A bar softens above the temperature at which its polymer goes rubbery.
A crystalline polymer melts above the temperature at which a needle sinks into it.
A polymer melts above its glass transition.
A polymer crystallises on cooling, below where it melted.
A bar yields before it breaks.
The ultimate stress is the highest the bar reached, so it is at least the stress at yield.
A bar bends harder than it pulls, because its outer fibre carries the load.
A bar deflects at a lower temperature under a heavier load, so one product's documents and its twins' sheets cannot put its HDT at 1.8 MPa above its HDT at 0.45 MPa.
The ultimate tensile strength is the highest stress on the stress-strain curve, so the stress at break cannot exceed it in the same test.
The strain at the maximum stress is reached on the way to break, so it cannot exceed the strain at break in the same test.
A semicrystalline bar loses its stiffness as its crystals melt, so it cannot deflect under load at a temperature above its melting point, whatever the load or the heat treatment.

A glassy bar loses its stiffness at its glass transition, so a bar that was not annealed cannot hold the 0.45 MPa load much above it; the margin is the scatter of the 98 PLA pairs in this database, whose glassy bars sit at most 5 °C above (D149).
